location.title: Location
location.description: City or area to search, e.g. "Kolkata, India" or "Salt Lake Sector V, Kolkata".

areas.title: Areas to sweep
areas.description: Run every search term separately against each area. This is the single most important setting for coverage: Google's local finder caps out near 100 results per query, so sweeping sub-areas is the only way past that ceiling. Leave empty to use either the single Location above or the built-in area list.

useBuiltInAreas.title: Use built-in Kolkata area list
useBuiltInAreas.description: Sweeps 46 built-in Kolkata/Howrah localities instead of one city-wide query. Needed for full coverage, but multiplies SERP usage by 46 - check the budget maths in the README first.

categories.title: Sectors to include
categories.description: Which sectors to search for and keep. Defaults to the five commercial-agency sectors. Data/AI, cybersecurity and game development are available but off by default; note that a software firm which merely mentions AI is still kept as software - only pure plays in an unselected sector are dropped.

searchTerms.title: Search terms
searchTerms.description: Optional override. Leave empty to use the phrase set for your selected sectors, which is usually better.

countryCode.title: Country
countryCode.description: Selects both the Google domain and the proxy exit country. Must match your target market or results come back for the wrong locale.

maxCompanies.title: Max companies
maxCompanies.description: Stop after this many unique companies. Set 0 for no limit (needed if you want everything).

maxLocalPagesPerTerm.title: Local finder pages per term
maxLocalPagesPerTerm.description: Each page yields roughly 20 businesses and costs one SERP request. 3 pages x 5 terms = 15 SERP requests for discovery.

serpBudget.title: SERP request budget
serpBudget.description: Hard cap on Google requests for this run, so you cannot accidentally drain the monthly SERP allowance (10,000 on the Creator plan). Set 0 for no cap.

itFilter.title: Apply sector filter
itFilter.description: Drops training institutes, recruitment agencies, repair shops and retailers, which Google's local finder mixes into these queries heavily. Rejections are tallied by reason in the run log.

requireWebsite.title: Only keep companies with a website
requireWebsite.description: No website means weaker founder, employee and type data. Turn on for a fully-enriched list.

minRating.title: Minimum Google rating
minRating.description: Optional, e.g. 4.5. Leave empty to keep all. Note: unrated new companies are dropped when this is set.

minReviews.title: Minimum number of reviews
minReviews.description: Optional. Filters out listings with little review history.

enrichFromWebsite.title: Crawl company websites
enrichFromWebsite.description: Reads each company's own site for founder, team size and service/product signals. Costs no SERP requests - this is direct HTTP.

enrichFounderFromSerp.title: Look up founder via Google
enrichFounderFromSerp.description: One SERP request per company, used only when the company's own website did not state a founder.

enrichEmployeesFromSerp.title: Look up employee count via Google
enrichEmployeesFromSerp.description: One SERP request per company. Reads the employee count out of the LinkedIn company page's Google snippet - it never fetches or logs into LinkedIn.

maxPagesPerSite.title: Max pages per website
maxPagesPerSite.description: Homepage plus this many About/Team/Services pages. Higher means better founder detection but slower runs.

concurrency.title: Concurrent website reads
concurrency.description: How many company websites to crawl at once. Does not affect SERP requests, which are always sequential and rate-limited.

requestTimeoutSecs.title: Per-request timeout (seconds)
requestTimeoutSecs.description: How long to wait for each request before giving up.

debugDumpHtml.title: Save raw Google HTML for debugging
debugDumpHtml.description: Saves the first local-results page per search term to the key-value store. Turn this on if results go empty - Google rotates its CSS class names, and the saved HTML is what you need to fix the selectors.
